name: Ricardo Villanueva
bio:
Ricardo's journey into motorsport analytics began unconventionally, far from the track. A former professor of statistics at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru, Ricardo became fascinated by the complex data streams generated by racing cars. He believed that deep statistical analysis could unlock hidden performance gains. He left academia to pursue his passion, initially volunteering his services to smaller racing teams before being noticed by Target Racing for his innovative data modeling techniques.

Ricardo is a lone wolf, preferring to work independently in his data lab, poring over telemetry and simulations. His approach is deeply analytical, often challenging conventional wisdom with data-driven insights. He is known for his ability to extract meaningful patterns from noisy data, identifying subtle areas for improvement that others miss. His visionary approach to data analysis helps the team make bolder strategic decisions. 

His experience with Target Racing has been transformative, pushing the boundaries of data analytics in motorsport. Despite his academic background, he's earned the respect of the pit crew and drivers, proving that passion and data can overcome any obstacle.

physical.description: Ricardo is a man of average height, with a slightly professorial demeanor and kind eyes that reflect his analytical mind.

quirks: Always carries a worn copy of 'Probability and Statistics' by DeGroot
Drinks copious amounts of mate tea throughout the day
Mumbles equations under his breath when deeply focused
